name: LF33ABDT-TR
title: LFXX very low-dropout 500 mA voltage regulators with inhibit
summary: The LFXX family are fixed positive linear regulators delivering up to 500 mA with 0.45 V of dropout and about 0.5 mA of quiescent current. Outputs run from 1.5 V to 12 V in ±1 %, ±1.5 % and ±2 % selections. The 5-lead PPAK version adds a logic shutdown input that drops the supply current to about 50 µA; the TO-220, TO-220FP and DPAK versions are three-terminal and always on. A 2.2 µF output capacitor keeps it stable, and current and thermal limits are built in. LF120CDT-TR is the 12 V, ±2 % part in DPAK on tape and reel.

circuits.title: Test circuit
circuits.description: The fixture the electrical tables are measured in: 0.1 µF across the input, 2.2 µF electrolytic across the output, and a switch that ties INHIBIT to the input supply. A low INHIBIT level is marked ON and a high level OFF.

circuits.title: Logic-controlled precision 3.3/5.0 V selectable output
circuits.description: An LF50 and an LF33 share one input and one output node. Two inverters in series drive the two INHIBIT pins in opposite phase, so only one regulator is on at a time: CTRL low gives 3.3 V, CTRL high gives 5.0 V, ±1 %, up to 0.5 A, from an input of 6 to 16 V.

circuits.title: Sequential multi-output supply
circuits.description: A battery and a power switch feed an LF33, an LF50 and an LF120. Each regulator's INHIBIT is driven by one Schmitt inverter of an HCF40106 whose input sits on an RC from the switched supply: the outputs come up one after another as each capacitor charges; the R and C values are chosen for the order wanted. The 1 kΩ across the switched supply is there to discharge the timing capacitors quickly.

circuits.title: Multiple supply with ON/OFF toggle switch
circuits.description: One push button switches an LF120 and an LF50 on and off together. The button clocks a D flip-flop (HCF4013) whose inverted output returns to D through 470 kΩ with 0.22 µF to ground, so each press toggles it; the same output drives both INHIBIT pins. The reset input is fed from the supply through 0.1 µF, with 100 kΩ and a 1N4148 to ground; the clock input has 10 nF and 100 kΩ to ground.
notes: The HCF4013 half uses pins D (5), CLK (3), S (6), R (4), Q (1) and Q_BAR (2); Q is left open and the supply pins are not shown.
The Vcc and INHIBIT lines run on to further regulators.

circuits.title: Basic inhibit functions: CMOS gate drive
circuits.description: A CMOS 4000-series inverter powered from VIN drives INHIBIT straight; it may do so over the whole temperature and voltage range. ON high turns the output on.

circuits.title: Basic inhibit functions: 5 V or 3 V logic drive
circuits.description: A TTL or HC-MOS inverter on its own +5 V supply drives INHIBIT straight; 5 V or 3 V logic, or a microcontroller, may do the same.

circuits.title: Basic inhibit functions: switch to ground
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ pull-up from VIN holds INHIBIT high; a switch to ground pulls it low. Switch closed: output on. Switch open: output off.

circuits.title: Basic inhibit functions: switch to the input
circuits.description: A switch from VIN pulls INHIBIT high; a 10 kΩ pull-down holds it low otherwise. Switch closed: output off. Switch open: output on. The 10 kΩ is for noisy surroundings and is usually left out.

circuits.title: Delayed turn-on
circuits.description: The output turns on a while after the power switch closes. 100 kΩ charges 22 µF from the switched supply; the HCF40106 Schmitt inverter between that node and INHIBIT keeps the regulator off until the capacitor has charged. With these values the delay is about 1.5 s typical. The 1 kΩ across the switched supply discharges the timing capacitor quickly.

circuits.title: Low voltage bulb blinker
circuits.description: An LF50 flashes a 6 V, 0.5 A lamp from 6 to 16 V. Its ground pin sits one 1N4148 drop above ground, with 1 kΩ from that node to ground. INHIBIT carries 47 µF to ground and 220 kΩ from the output. The 47 µF sets how fast the lamp blinks.

operation.text: LFXX is a family of fixed positive low-dropout regulators rated to 500 mA. The code after LF gives the output: 15 = 1.5 V up to 120 = 12 V. AB parts hold ±1 % at 25 °C, AC parts ±1.5 % and C parts ±2 %. The family covers outputs of 1.5, 1.8, 2.5, 3.3, 4.7, 5, 6, 8, 8.5, 9 and 12 V; order codes exist for all of them except 4.7 V.

The 5-lead PPAK adds a TTL-compatible shutdown input on pin 2. Pulled high (VIH 2 V min) it turns the regulator off and the supply current falls to about 50 µA typical (70 µA on the 6 V and higher parts); pulled low (VIL 0.8 V max) the regulator runs, drawing 0.5 mA typical with no load (0.7 mA on the 6 V and higher parts). The three-lead TO-220, TO-220FP and DPAK parts perform the same but are always on. Shutting part of a board down this way saves power in standby.
Dropout is 0.45 V; typical figures are 0.2 V at 200 mA and 0.4 V at 500 mA. Low dropout and low supply current suit battery-powered, low-noise and low-power designs.

The regulator is stable with an output capacitor of 2.2 µF. The electrical tables give the output capacitance as 2 µF minimum, 10 µF typical, over an ESR of 0.1 to 10 Ω and loads of 0 to 500 mA. All tables are measured with 0.1 µF at the input and 2.2 µF at the output.

Output current and thermal limiting are internal; output current and power dissipation are internally limited in the absolute ratings. The short-circuit current of a 3.3 V part settles near 1.15 A above about 3 V of input.
The input is rated to 40 V. With the input between 18 V and 40 V the regulator is shut down; the operating input range ends at 16 V.
On TO-220, DPAK and PPAK the tab is electrically at GND.

The -TRY order codes in DPAK and PPAK (1.8, 2.5, 3.3, 5.0, 8.0 and 8.5 V) are automotive-grade parts qualified to AEC-Q100 over -40 °C to 125 °C, with PAT, SYL and SBL statistical tests applied. Their electrical tables are specified over Ta = -40 to 125 °C.
